links.outcome: Accuracy and citation fidelity of retrieval-grounded assistant versus ungrounded frontier LLMs on oncology vignettes
links.effect: Grounded Aprilio scored 100% accuracy vs 97-99% for most others and 89% for Qwen3 Max. Citations evaluable for claim support in 97/100 responses vs 20 for GPT-5.6 Terra and 5 or fewer for the rest. 55% of Aprilio citations substantiated claims vs 15% for the next best.
links.quote: Notably, 55% of responses generated by the Aprilio model carried citations which were confirmed to directly substantiate its assertions, whereas only 15% of citations from the next-best-performing model substantiated its claims.

links.outcome: Existence and validity of citations in LLM-generated oncology answers
links.effect: GPT-5.6 Terra produced four non-existent or erroneous citations. Perplexity Sonar Pro and Qwen3 Max left only one and twelve citations respectively. One model cited a patent-petition document. Other models left almost no locatable citations.
links.quote: As these models were not prompted specifically to perform an online search, all but one model (GPT-5.6 Terra) reliably did so, although four of the citations it provided were non-existent or erroneous.

unlisted_practices: Neuro-symbolic intent extraction and source scoring (recency, authority, indication match, relevance) for retrieval ranking

screen.reason: The study introduces and benchmarks a novel retrieval architecture (Grounded Ontogenic Retrieval / Aprilio system) against general-purpose LLMs on 100 oncology clinical questions; developing and benchmarking a new architecture or tool is not a deployment practice test.
